paper.task: Given an input sequence x, retrieve the top-K text documents z with a dense retriever and generate the target sequence y with a seq2seq generator conditioned on x and z, marginalizing over the retrieved documents (also usable for sequence classification by treating the class as a target sequence of length one).

components.name: input sequence x
components.what: the input / query sequence; used to retrieve documents and as context for the generator

provenance.quote: We explore RAG models, which use the input sequence x to retrieve text documents z

components.name: retriever
components.what: p_η(z|x): DPR-based bi-encoder that returns a top-K truncated distribution over text passages given the query x; initialized from a pre-trained DPR bi-encoder

provenance.quote: (i) a retriever p η (z|x) with parameters η that returns (top-K truncated) distributions over text passages given a query x

components.name: query encoder
components.what: BERT_q (BERT_BASE) mapping x to the dense query representation q(x); fine-tuned during training

provenance.quote: and q(x) a query representation produced by a query encoder, also based on BERT BASE

components.name: document encoder
components.what: BERT_d (BERT_BASE) mapping a document z to the dense representation d(z); used to build the document index; kept fixed during training

provenance.quote: where d(z) is a dense representation of a document produced by a BERT BASE document encoder

components.name: Maximum Inner Product Search
components.what: computes top-k(p_η(·|x)): the k documents with highest prior p_η(z|x) ∝ exp(d(z)ᵀq(x)); approximately solvable in sub-linear time

provenance.quote: Calculating top-k(p η (·|x)), the list of k documents z with highest prior probability p η (z|x), is a Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS) problem

components.name: text passages
components.what: the text documents z the retriever searches over, encoded by the document encoder (the corpus is not named in this text)

provenance.quote: returns (top-K truncated) distributions over text passages given a query x

components.name: document index
components.what: index of document representations d(z) built with the pre-trained DPR bi-encoder; the non-parametric memory; kept fixed during training

provenance.quote: We refer to the document index as the non-parametric memory.

components.name: retrieved documents z
components.what: the top-K retrieved documents, treated as a latent variable

provenance.quote: Concretely, the top K documents are retrieved using the retriever

components.name: concatenate
components.what: joins the input x with a retrieved document z to form the generator's input

provenance.quote: To combine the input x with the retrieved content z when generating from BART, we simply concatenate them.

components.name: BART generator
components.what: p_θ(y_i|x, z, y_1:i−1): BART-large, a pre-trained seq2seq transformer with 400M parameters; the parametric memory; fine-tuned during training

provenance.quote: We use BART-large [32], a pre-trained seq2seq transformer [58] with 400M parameters.

components.name: marginalize
components.what: sums the generator's per-document probabilities weighted by p_η(z|x) over the top-K documents: RAG-Sequence marginalizes once per output sequence (same document for the whole sequence), RAG-Token per output token (a different document per token); the two are equivalent for sequence classification

provenance.quote: We propose two models that marginalize over the latent documents in different ways to produce a distribution over generated text.

components.name: target sequence y
components.what: the generated output sequence, with probability p(y|x)

provenance.quote: use them as additional context when generating the target sequence y

components.name: negative marginal log-likelihood
components.what: Σ_j −log p(y_j|x_j) over input/output training pairs (x_j, y_j), minimized with stochastic gradient descent with Adam

provenance.quote: minimize the negative marginal log-likelihood of each target, j − log p(y j |x j ) using stochastic gradient descent with Adam [28]

train_vs_infer.what: Training: the document encoder BERT_d and the document index are kept fixed; only the query encoder BERT_q and the BART generator are fine-tuned

provenance.quote: keep the document encoder (and index) fixed, only fine-tuning the query encoder BERT q and the BART generator

train_vs_infer.what: Training: retriever and generator are trained jointly on input/output pairs, with no direct supervision on which document should be retrieved

provenance.quote: We jointly train the retriever and generator components without any direct supervision on what document should be retrieved.

train_vs_infer.what: Test time, RAG-Token: the per-token marginalized transition probability p′_θ(y_i|x, y_1:i−1) is plugged into a standard beam decoder

provenance.quote: To decode, we can plug p 0 θ (y i |x, y 1:i−1 ) into a standard beam decoder.

train_vs_infer.what: Test time, RAG-Sequence 'Thorough Decoding': beam search per document z; for each hypothesis missing from a document's beam an additional forward pass is run, generator probabilities are multiplied by p_η(z|x) and summed across beams

provenance.quote: Instead, we run beam search for each document z, scoring each hypothesis using p θ (y i |x, z, y 1:i−1 ). … we run an additional forward pass for each document z for which y does not appear in the beam, multiply generator probability with p η (z|x) and then sum the probabilities across beams for the marginals. We refer to this decoding procedure as “Thorough Decoding.”

train_vs_infer.what: Test time, RAG-Sequence 'Fast Decoding': p_θ(y|x, z_i) is approximated as 0 for hypotheses not generated in z_i's beam, avoiding the additional forward passes

provenance.quote: we can make a further approximation that p θ (y|x, z i ) ≈ 0 where y was not generated during beam search from x, z i . This avoids the need to run additional forward passes once the candidate set Y has been generated. We refer to this decoding procedure as “Fast Decoding.”

contributions.text: RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token: two models that marginalize over the latent retrieved documents in different ways — the same document for the whole output sequence vs a possibly different document for each target token

provenance.quote: We propose two models that marginalize over the latent documents in different ways to produce a distribution over generated text. In one approach, RAG-Sequence, the model uses the same document to predict each target token. The second approach, RAG-Token, can predict each target token based on a different document.

unclear: The text says 'As shown in Figure 1' for the retriever and generator; the figure is not available in this blind run and nothing was taken from it.
A footnote about the open-sourced code interrupts the sentence defining the generator (between 'parametrized' and 'by θ'); it was read as one sentence.

The display equations are fragmented in extraction (summation/product symbols appear as stray 'N', 'Y', 'X', 'P' lines; the pieces of the RAG-Sequence equation are out of order). The marginalization structure is taken from the prose; equation lines are quoted as they appear.

Novelty: the only explicit claim is 'We propose two models that marginalize over the latent documents in different ways'. The retriever (based on DPR, initialized from a pre-trained DPR bi-encoder) and generator (pre-trained BART-large) are recorded as reused; only the marginalization is recorded as proposed. RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token are recorded as two variants inside the one 'marginalize' component, not as separate boxes; the whole RAG model is not a box.

The retriever is reused, but its parts (query encoder, document encoder, MIPS) are recorded because the text describes them and the training rule (query encoder fine-tuned, document encoder and index fixed) is stated per part.

That MIPS searches the document index is implied (the index is built with the bi-encoder, p_η(z|x) ∝ exp(d(z)ᵀq(x)), and top-k is a MIPS problem) but never stated in one sentence; doc_index -> mips is recorded on that basis.

Whether the document index sits inside the retriever is not stated: the pre-trained bi-encoder is used 'to initialize our retriever and to build the document index', and the index is called the non-parametric memory (parallel to the generator's parametric memory), so it is recorded outside the retriever (parent null).
The corpus the text passages come from is not named in this text, nor how documents are split into passages.
The number of retrieved documents K is not given in this text.
How x and z are concatenated (order, separator) is not stated.

The previous tokens y_1:i−1 fed to the generator are recorded as output_y -> generator; the text does not say whether they are the ground-truth target (training) or the decoded hypothesis (test time).
The loss uses p(y_j|x_j) from the marginalization; the text does not describe the ground-truth target y_j as a separate input to the loss.

Gradient edges (loss -> query encoder, loss -> generator) follow from 'only fine-tuning the query encoder BERT q and the BART generator'; the text does not spell out that the query encoder's gradient arrives through p_η(z|x) in the marginal likelihood.

Decoding procedures (beam decoder for RAG-Token; Thorough / Fast Decoding for RAG-Sequence) are recorded under train_vs_infer, not as components; whether an overview draws them is left to the design step.
